title: Equal counts of the bad size-$k$ restrictions
statement: Let $f$ be a Boolean function on $n$ variables and fix natural numbers $d$ and $k$. For a restriction $\rho$ on these variables, write $f|_\rho$ for the restricted function that sends a point $x$ to the value of $f$ obtained by fixing each assigned coordinate as $\rho$ prescribes and reading each free coordinate off $x$, and call $\rho$ bad for $f$ at depth $d$ when the decision-tree depth of $f|_\rho$ is strictly greater than $d$. Then the number of restrictions that have exactly $k$ free variables and are bad for $f$ at depth $d$ is the same whether these are counted within the collection of all restrictions with exactly $k$ free variables or within the collection of all restrictions on the $n$ variables that both have exactly $k$ free variables and are bad for $f$ at depth $d$.
hypotheses_covered: a Boolean function f on n variables
a number k of free variables
replaced:
For a function $f$ and parameters $d, k$, the number of size-$k$ restrictions
$\rho$ with $\mathrm{dtDepth}(f|_\rho) > d$ equals the number of restrictions
that are $k$-restrictions and are bad for $f$ at depth $d$ in the counting
switching-lemma sense.
